dedupe_keys.name: equity constrained dispatching model of emergency medical services netlogo agent based comparison of ambulance dispatching policies

description: This agent-based model compares ways of dispatching ambulances when an emergency medical service must also be fair to patients and to crews. It was written in NetLogo by Sreekanth V. K. and Ram Babu Roy and accompanies their 2017 paper on equity-constrained dispatching models for emergency medical services in Team Performance Management. Calls arrive from several locations and ambulances are based at several stations. The model tests two policies, one that maximises reward and one based on a Markov decision process, under four equity constraints, two on the patients' side and two on the providers' side, extending earlier work by McLay and Mayorga. Version 1.2.0 of the code is available as a free download from the CoMSES library under the GPL-3.0 licence. Caveats: the call and station layout is stylised, not taken from a real service, and the library page gives no validation. Coverage is general, not tied to one country. Simulation uses: comparing dispatch rules and the effect of fairness requirements on response performance, as a building block for emergency service resilience studies. Related records: the NEMSIS research dataset (data-nemsis-research-dataset) holds real EMS activations that could calibrate such a model.
inputs: Call locations and ambulance base locations
Dispatching policy (maximum reward or Markov decision process) and equity constraints
name: Equity Constrained Dispatching Model of Emergency Medical Services: NetLogo agent-based comparison of ambulance dispatching policies
outputs: Performance of each dispatching policy under patient-side and provider-side equity constraints
